outcome.technical:
SCHEMA READER: new plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_json_schema.py, which reads the published schema with the stdlib alone. All five obligations are met: an inline --selftest stub with the cases in tests/test__json_schema.py, safe_stdio first, an entry in _deps.LAYERS next to _manifest_vocab, a PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE tree line and section with the module-map fence matching `_deps.py --render`, and PATH_PREAMBLE. test__output sc11/sc13 and test__manifest_vocab mv36 list it. It checks type, enum, const, items, oneOf/anyOf/allOf, pattern, properties, required, additionalProperties, min/maxLength, minimum/maximum and exclusiveMinimum/Maximum. Any other keyword is returned as unread, never as a pass. ecma_pattern no longer compiles with re.ASCII: it translates \d and \w to ASCII classes, keeps \s Unicode-wide and reads a trailing $ as \Z. A pattern that will not compile becomes an unread `pattern` instead of a re.error. load_document refuses a schema that is not an object or holds a $ref that names nothing, and crossrefs.load_plan_schema also refuses one whose bug item has no properties.

THE FOLD: the bug-only reader in _manifest_crossrefs now calls _json_schema and keeps its crossrefs.bugs.schema-* codes and its deduplication against the hand-written bug checks.

WHOLE PLAN: _manifest_rules._check_schema applies the schema to the whole plan. bugs are left to _check_bugs. Each failure is a rules.schema.<kind> WARNING naming 4.0.0, not a finding, because COMPATIBILITY.md promises 'Validation stays additive'. A schema line is not repeated where a hand-written finding already opens with the same path. validate() reads the schema once; with schema=None a failed read is one warning. validate-manifest.py --strict moves every schema line into the findings, so it exits 1 exactly where ajv rejects. I checked that against a real `ajv-cli --spec=draft2020 --all-errors` run over four planted plans and the paths were identical; the starter, the dogfood plan and acme have no schema lines and pass --strict.

BROKEN INSTALL: _manifest_rules.bound_validator() loads the schema once and binds it. set-priority, derive-phase-gate, _panel_write.apply_composition and _proposals._revalidate now validate through it, so an unreadable schema refuses their write instead of the fallback only warning. COMPATIBILITY.md names the writers that still use the fallback: merge-manifest, repair-commits, repair-tests-add, migrate-json-encoding and migrate-manifest.

LIST/OBJECT IDS (validate() never raises): _manifest_vocab._require_fields reports a list or object id as a finding naming 'id'. Number ids are left to the schema warning, because they validated before. _manifest_crossrefs:
- removed the unused json/re imports;
- _keyed() makes _index_bugs and _index_decisions index only string ids;
- _check_unique_ids and _cycle_findings.add_edge skip list and object ids;
- new findings crossrefs.bugs.taskid-string and crossrefs.bugs.bugid-string.
_manifest_phases skips list and object phase and task ids when indexing. _manifest_io.keyable_id now guards status_index, tasks_by_id, phase_of_task, effective_bug_status and _fix_task.

CORRECTION to the earlier return: a list or object bug taskId DID raise before this fix. The TypeError came from _manifest_io.effective_bug_status, at `task_by_id.get(tid)`, reached through derived_disagreements; mc47 showed it.

ado.id 7.0 is still refused, and the finding now says the schema admits it and why it is refused: _ado_drift._collect:282 and read-ado-links.py:488 keep only int ids. _panel_state._cores: both '(twice)' counts deleted. The finding $def keys were already present (commit 3994386a).

COST, two runs 20 s apart: validate() on docs/audit/audit-plan.json (125 phases, 841 tasks) took 27-32 ms before and 97-102 ms after; validate-manifest.py wall time was 0.19 s on both runs.

GATES: sweep exit 0, 330/330 files ok. ruff and vermin exit 0. The suites I touched are all green: test__json_schema 11/11, test_validate_manifest 55/55, test__manifest_crossrefs 97/97, test__manifest_io 186/186, test__manifest_rules 165/165, test__manifest_vocab 71/71, test__manifest_phases 122/122, test_set_priority 39/39, test_derive_phase_gate 31/31, test__panel_write 268/268, test__proposals 62/62, test__output 250/250.
outcome.descriptive: validate-manifest now applies the published schema to the whole plan, as warnings in 3.x and as findings under --strict, matching ajv on the real and planted plans. Every write site touched here binds the schema, so a broken install refuses the write. A list or object id is now a named finding and no longer an internal-validator-error raise.
